Platyhelminthes has organ level with an incomplete digestive system having a single opening for both mouth and anus.
Sponges show which type of body plan?
A plane passing through the central axis dividing the body into identical halves defines
Radial symmetry: any plane through the central axis produces identical halves.
Insects and chordates are bilaterally symmetrical.
Coelenterates have two germ layers (diploblastic) with mesoglea in between.
Animals in which mesoderm occurs as scattered pouches between ectoderm and endoderm are called
This scattered mesoderm pattern defines pseudocoelomates, e.g. Aschelminthes.
Platyhelminthes are triploblastic but lack a body cavity, i.e., acoelomate.
Which of these phyla is coelomate?
Annelida possesses a true mesoderm-lined coelom.
Metameric segmentation is best exemplified by
Earthworm shows external and internal segmentation with repeated organs (metamerism).

Sponges have which level of organisation?
Porifera exhibits cellular level of organisation.
Water enters the body of a sponge through
Water enters through minute pores called ostia.
The cells lining the spongocoel and canals in sponges are called
Choanocytes (collar cells) line the spongocoel and canals.
The skeleton of sponges consists of
Sponge skeletons are made of spicules or spongin fibres.
The larva found in Sycon is the
Sycon shows amphiblastula larva; Leucosolenia shows parenchymula larva.
The single opening of the gastro-vascular cavity in coelenterates is the
The hypostome is the single opening surrounded by tentacles.
Nematocysts are the stinging capsules in cnidoblasts/cnidocytes.
The sessile, cylindrical body form of coelenterates is called
Polyp is the sessile, cylindrical form, e.g. Hydra.
Alternation of generation in coelenterates is termed
Metagenesis is the alternation between polyp and medusa forms, e.g. Obelia.
Which coelenterate exhibits both polyp and medusa stages with metagenesis?
Obelia shows polyp producing medusa asexually and medusa forming polyp sexually.
The locomotory organs in Ctenophora are
Eight rows of ciliated comb plates are the locomotory organs.
Ctenophores can emit light, i.e., bioluminescence.
Ctenophores are hermaphrodite; sexes are not separate.
Their dorso-ventrally flattened body gives the name flatworms.

Taenia is the tapeworm, a parasite in pigs and humans.
Planaria is known for its high regeneration capacity.
Their circular cross-section body gives the name round worms.
Wuchereria causes which disease in humans?
Dioecious with females longer than males
Aschelminthes are dioecious; females are typically longer than males.
In America, the common vector for Wuchereria (filarial worm) is
Culex is the common vector for filariasis in America; Anopheles is common in Africa.
The excretory organs of Annelida are called
Parapodia are lateral appendages that aid swimming in aquatic annelids.
The largest phylum in Animalia is
Arthropoda is the largest phylum, comprising over two-thirds of known species.
Malpighian tubules are the excretory organs in arthropods.
The coelom filled with blood in arthropods is called
Haemocoel is characteristic of the open circulatory system in Arthropoda.
Which vector transmits Zika virus and can cause avian malaria in birds?
Culex transmits Zika virus in humans and avian malaria in birds.
Mollusca is the ___ largest phylum among invertebrates.
Mollusca is the second largest phylum in Animalia among invertebrates.
The feeding organ in most molluscs is called
Radula is the file-like feeding organ in molluscs.
The space between the visceral hump and the mantle is called
The mantle cavity houses feather-like gills.
The excretory organs in molluscs are
Metanephridia (1-2 pairs of kidneys) perform excretion in molluscs.
The distinctive locomotory system in Echinodermata is the
Water vascular/ambulacral system helps in locomotion and feeding.
In Echinodermata, the mouth is located on the
Mouth is on the ventral (lower) side; anus is dorsal (upper) side.
The larval stage seen in Echinodermata development is
Bipinnaria larva is the free-swimming larval stage in Echinodermata.
Hemichordata was earlier considered a sub-phylum of
Hemichordata was earlier placed as a sub-phylum of chordates.
The excretory organ in Hemichordata is the
Proboscis gland performs excretion in hemichordates.
Balanoglossus is also called the tongue worm or acorn worm.
The three fundamental features of Chordata are
Notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, gill slits
These three features define Phylum Chordata.
Cyclostomes have a mouth that is
Cyclostomes have a sucking, circular, jawless mouth.
Cyclostomes are ectoparasitic on other fishes.
The endoskeleton in Chondrichthyes is made of
Chondrichthyes must swim continuously because they lack
Absence of an air bladder means they sink if they stop swimming.
Torpedo has electric organs generating 8-220 volts.
The gills in Osteichthyes are covered by
Operculum covers the four pairs of gills in bony fish.
Buoyancy in bony fish is provided by
The air bladder provides buoyancy in Osteichthyes.
A heterocercal caudal fin, absence of air bladder, and placoid scales are characteristic of
These are hallmark features of Chondrichthyes.
The common opening for digestive, excretory and reproductive tracts in amphibians is the
The cloaca serves as the common opening in amphibians.
Amphibian heart has two auricles and one ventricle.
Amphibians can respire through gills, lungs, and skin.
Reptiles are characterised by locomotion that is
Reptiles show a creeping or crawling mode of locomotion.
Which reptile has a four-chambered heart?
Crocodiles uniquely have a four-chambered heart among reptiles.
Snakes and lizards periodically shed their
Snakes and lizards shed scales as a skin cast (ecdysis).
Which of these is a flightless bird?
The additional digestive chambers found in birds are
Birds have a crop and gizzard as extra digestive chambers.

The unique characteristic feature of mammals is the presence of
Mammary glands producing milk are unique to mammals.
Which mammal is an exception, being oviparous?
Platypus is an oviparous mammal, unlike most viviparous mammals.
External ears in mammals are called
Pinnae are the external ears found only in mammals.
Which superclass includes Amphibia, Reptilia, Aves and Mammalia?
Tetrapoda (bear limbs) includes these four classes.
Agnatha differs from Gnathostomata mainly in the
Agnatha lacks jaws while Gnathostomata bears jaws.
The presence or absence of a body cavity lined by mesoderm is used to classify animals as coelomate, pseudocoelomate or _____.
Animals lacking a mesoderm-lined body cavity altogether are called acoelomate, e.g. Platyhelminthes.
In sponges, water enters through minute pores called ostia and exits through a large opening called the _____.
The osculum is the large excurrent opening through which water leaves a sponge.
Stinging cells present on the tentacles of coelenterates that aid in capture of prey are called _____.
Cnidoblasts (cnidocytes) contain nematocysts used for defence, anchorage and prey capture.
The specialised excretory cells found in Platyhelminthes, which help in osmoregulation, are called _____.
Flame cells (solenocytes) are the excretory/osmoregulatory units in flatworms.
Aschelminthes may be free-living, aquatic or terrestrial, and free-living forms are commonly found in _____.
Free-living Aschelminthes commonly inhabit moist soil.
Lateral appendages that help aquatic annelids like Nereis in swimming are called _____.
Parapodia are the lateral appendages used for swimming in aquatic annelids.
The excretory organs of most insects, which remove nitrogenous waste from the haemolymph, are called _____.
Malpighian tubules are the characteristic excretory structures of arthropods.
The file-like rasping structure used by most molluscs for feeding is called the _____.
The radula is the characteristic feeding organ of molluscs.
The distinctive system in Echinodermata used for locomotion, feeding and respiration is the _____.
The water vascular (ambulacral) system is unique to echinoderms.
A flexible rod-like structure that provides support along the back in chordate embryos is called the _____.
The notochord is one of the three defining features of chordates.
In bony fish, the gills are covered by a bony flap called the _____.
The operculum covers and protects the gills in Osteichthyes.
Mammals uniquely nourish their young using milk secreted by _____.
Mammary glands, the defining feature of Mammalia, produce milk for the young.
If a sponge is cut into small pieces and each piece regenerates into a new sponge, which property of Porifera does this best demonstrate?
Sponges show remarkable powers of regeneration due to the totipotent nature of their archaeocytes.
A starfish is observed using its tube feet to move, capture prey, and exchange gases — all powered by one internal system. Which system is this?
The water vascular system, unique to echinoderms, powers locomotion, feeding, and respiration via tube feet.
A marine biologist examines a fish and finds it has a cartilaginous endoskeleton, placoid scales, and no operculum. This fish most likely belongs to
Cartilaginous endoskeleton, placoid scales, and absence of an operculum are hallmark features of Chondrichthyes.
In the context of Phylum Porifera, the term most directly associated with the stated diagnostic feature is _____.
cellular organisation is the intended term; it is a key association for Phylum Porifera.
In the context of Phylum Platyhelminthes, the term most directly associated with the stated diagnostic feature is _____.
acoelomate is the intended term; it is a key association for Phylum Platyhelminthes.
In the context of Phylum Arthropoda, the term most directly associated with the stated diagnostic feature is _____.
haemocoel is the intended term; it is a key association for Phylum Arthropoda.
In the context of Phylum Hemichordata, the term most directly associated with the stated diagnostic feature is _____.
lack true notochord is the intended term; it is a key association for Phylum Hemichordata.
In the context of Class Chondrichthyes, the term most directly associated with the stated diagnostic feature is _____.
lack air bladder is the intended term; it is a key association for Class Chondrichthyes.
In the context of Class Reptilia, the term most directly associated with the stated diagnostic feature is _____.
Crocodilus is the intended term; it is a key association for Class Reptilia.
In the context of Summary — Salient Features of Phyla, the term most directly associated with the stated diagnostic feature is _____.
cellular versus tissue is the intended term; it is a key association for Summary — Salient Features of Phyla.
In the context of Segmentation and Notochord, the term most directly associated with the stated diagnostic feature is _____.
earthworm is the intended term; it is a key association for Segmentation and Notochord.
In the context of Phylum Ctenophora, the term most directly associated with the stated diagnostic feature is _____.
colloblasts is the intended term; it is a key association for Phylum Ctenophora.
In the context of Phylum Annelida, the term most directly associated with the stated diagnostic feature is _____.
nephridia is the intended term; it is a key association for Phylum Annelida.
In the context of Phylum Echinodermata, the term most directly associated with the stated diagnostic feature is _____.
external fertilisation is the intended term; it is a key association for Phylum Echinodermata.
In the context of Class Cyclostomata, the term most directly associated with the stated diagnostic feature is _____.
Petromyzon is the intended term; it is a key association for Class Cyclostomata.
In the context of Class Amphibia, the term most directly associated with the stated diagnostic feature is _____.
land and water is the intended term; it is a key association for Class Amphibia.
Which criterion separates animals with cellular level of organisation from those with tissue level of organisation?
Level of organisation is a fundamental basis of animal classification.
An animal that can be divided into equal halves by any plane passing through its central axis shows:
Radially symmetrical animals can be divided into similar halves by any plane through the central axis.
Repeated serial arrangement of similar body units along the longitudinal axis is called:
Metamerism is true segmentation into repeated serial units.
The water current in a sponge finally leaves the body through the:
Water enters through ostia, reaches the spongocoel/canal system and exits through the osculum.
The stinging capsules characteristic of cnidarians are called:
Cnidoblasts contain nematocysts used for anchorage, defence and capture of prey.
Locomotion in ctenophores is brought about by:
Eight rows of ciliary comb plates bring about locomotion in ctenophores.

Flatworms are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic and acoelomate.
Excretion in earthworm is carried out by:
Nephridia are the excretory organs of annelids such as earthworm.
The body appendages of arthropods are characteristically:
Jointed appendages are the most characteristic feature of Arthropoda.
The rasping feeding organ found in most molluscs is the:
The radula is a rasping feeding organ; it is absent in bivalves.
In molluscs, the soft, spongy fold of body wall that covers the visceral hump and secretes the shell is the:
The mantle is a body-wall fold that secretes the shell and encloses the mantle cavity.
The water vascular system of echinoderms principally helps in:
Tube feet of the water vascular system function in locomotion, feeding and respiration.
The body of Balanoglossus is divided into:
Hemichordates have a characteristic proboscis, collar and trunk.
Why are hemichordates placed in a separate phylum rather than in Chordata?
They have no organ-system level of organisation.
Hemichordates have pharyngeal gill slits but do not possess a true notochord.
Which is NOT a characteristic chordate feature?
Chordates have a dorsal hollow nerve cord, unlike the usual ventral solid cord of non-chordates.
A tunicate larva has a notochord that is present only in its tail. It belongs to:
In urochordates, the notochord is present only in the larval tail.
Cyclostomes are jawless vertebrates with a circular sucking mouth.
The scales of cartilaginous fishes are:
Chondrichthyans such as sharks possess placoid scales.
The bony flap covering the gills of most Osteichthyes is the:
In bony fishes, four pairs of gills are covered by an operculum.

The air bladder helps most Osteichthyes maintain buoyancy.
Amphibians generally have a heart with:
Most amphibians have a three-chambered heart.
The skin of reptiles is characteristically:
Dry and cornified with epidermal scales/scutes
Reptilian skin is dry, cornified and generally bears epidermal scales or scutes.
The body of birds is generally covered with:
Feathers are the diagnostic body covering of Aves.
In birds, the large keel on the sternum provides attachment for:
The keeled sternum gives attachment to powerful flight muscles.
The structure that provides nourishment to young ones in female mammals is the:
Mammary glands are the defining feature of Mammalia.
Which combination is diagnostic of Mammalia?
Hair, external ear pinnae and mammary glands
Placoid scales, gill slits and cartilage
Hair, mammary glands and usually external ear pinnae distinguish mammals.
Which phylum is the largest in Kingdom Animalia?
Arthropoda is the largest phylum of animals.
